title: Multiplatform Build and Release knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the main idea of “Multiplatform Build and Release”?
options: Kotlin Multiplatform organizes shared logic and target-specific implementations through source sets; only APIs available for every configured target belong in common code.
It makes versioning, input validation, and testing unnecessary.
It means all Kotlin libraries and platform APIs behave identically.
It removes the need to understand types or runtime behavior.
questions.answer_key: Kotlin Multiplatform organizes shared logic and target-specific implementations through source sets; only APIs available for every configured target belong in common code.
questions.explanation: The reliable answer is grounded in the lesson’s main principle: Kotlin Multiplatform organizes shared logic and target-specific implementations through source sets; only APIs available for every configured target belong in common code. questions.prompt: Which learning/debugging practice is most reliable for “Multiplatform Build and Release”?
options: Change several unrelated parts at once and keep the result that looks plausible.
Ignore warnings and suppress failures before identifying the cause.
Assume the compiler or toolchain is broken without reducing the example.
Use a minimal reproducible example, compare the actual result with the expected result, and check the target/version assumptions.
questions.answer_key: Use a minimal reproducible example, compare the actual result with the expected result, and check the target/version assumptions.
questions.explanation: A minimal reproducible example and version-aware testing separate a real behavior from a mistaken assumption. Review the example and one relevant edge case before moving on.

questions.prompt: Which claim should a learner avoid when applying “Multiplatform Build and Release”?
options: Expose every internal implementation detail to every caller.
Never inspect the official API reference for the selected target.
Multiplatform Build and Release removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.
Treat draft or experimental features as universally stable.
questions.answer_key: Multiplatform Build and Release removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.
questions.explanation: The misconception to avoid is: Multiplatform Build and Release removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version. Review the example and one relevant edge case before moving on.
